scope: Independent source review of selected-workspace Source recognition and local Saved/Open/retry behavior; no browser or test execution in this lane
confirmed_from_source: Recognition returns unknown when no workspace is selected or its selection cannot be read, and only queries docproc with an exact organization_id predicate (queries.ts:620-655).
The recognition hook clears an old claim on workspace changes and ignores late lookup answers; a broadcast only triggers a fresh lookup (use-page-recognition.ts:33-100).
The local Saved button and Open this Source link require the landed organization's id to match the selected workspace and the same unedited capture (ScrapeView.tsx:88-100, 716-740).
A late landed Save in A stays hidden while B is selected, and the capture remains in memory. The added guards cover this success ordering (save-never-loses-input.test.tsx:384-458).

findings.title: An older refused Save can overwrite a newer workspace's retry capture
findings.evidence: ScrapeView.tsx:124-131 releases the Save control on a workspace switch, allowing B to Save while A remains in flight. On refusal, saveCaptureAsSource always calls upsertUnsaved (save-capture.ts:291-302). upsertUnsaved keys solely by canonical URL and replaces the stored row with whichever refusal completes last (save-capture.ts:208-224). Thus A starts, the person switches to B and edits/saves, B refuses and queues the B version, then A refuses late: the queue now contains A's older prepared content and organizationId. The current guard at save-never-loses-input.test.tsx:433-458 resolves A successfully, so it does not cover this ordering. retryUnsavedCapture's refusal also unconditionally upserts its stale row (save-capture.ts:315-333).
findings.required_repair: Give queued attempts a monotonic revision or equivalent compare-and-swap rule so a late earlier refusal cannot replace a newer capture or workspace retry. Cover A-late-refusal after B-refusal with changed article text, assert the queued body and organization remain B, and cover stale retry refusal against a newer queued edit.
